atlantic.name: Atlantic Ocean
atlantic.hint: Look west of Ireland, England, France and Portugal.
atlantic.fact: The Atlantic lies west of Europe.

north.name: North Sea
north.hint: Look between Britain and the coast of northern mainland Europe.
north.fact: The North Sea lies east of Britain.

adriatic.name: Adriatic Sea
adriatic.hint: Find the narrow sea east of Italy.
adriatic.fact: The Adriatic connects Venice with the Mediterranean.

mediterranean.name: Mediterranean Sea
mediterranean.hint: Look south of Europe, between Europe and North Africa.
mediterranean.fact: Mediterranean sea routes connected European, African and Asian ports.

black.name: Black Sea
black.hint: Look north of Anatolia, in the east of the map.
black.fact: The Black Sea lies north of Anatolia.

ireland.name: Ireland
ireland.hint: Find the island west of Britain.
ireland.fact: Ireland lies west of Britain. This identifies the island, which was not a single united kingdom in 1400.

scotland.name: Scotland
scotland.hint: Find the northern part of Britain.
scotland.fact: Scotland was a separate kingdom during the medieval period.

england.name: England
england.fact: The Renaissance later developed in England, including literature and theatre.

france.name: France
france.hint: Look across the Channel from England.
france.fact: Artists and ideas travelled between Italy and France.

castile.name: Spain (Castile)
castile.hint: Find the large kingdom east of Portugal. Spain was divided into kingdoms.
castile.fact: Castile was one of several Iberian kingdoms. It is not identical to all of modern Spain.

granada.name: Granada
granada.hint: Find the small kingdom along the southern edge of Iberia.
granada.fact: Granada was an Islamic kingdom until its conquest in 1492.

portugal.name: Portugal
portugal.hint: Look along the western edge of Iberia.

hre.name: Holy Roman Empire
hre.hint: Find the large central region north of the Italian peninsula.
hre.fact: The Holy Roman Empire included many territories and cities. It was not modern Germany.

genoa.name: Genoa
genoa.hint: Look on the northwestern coast of Italy.
genoa.fact: Genoa was a maritime republic. Its merchants and wealthy families supported trade and the arts.

papal.name: Papal States
papal.hint: Look in central Italy, around Rome.
papal.fact: The Papal States were territories ruled by the pope.

naples.name: Kingdom of Naples
naples.hint: Find the southern part of the Italian mainland.
naples.fact: The Kingdom of Naples occupied much of southern mainland Italy.

sicily.name: Kingdom of Sicily
sicily.hint: Find the island just below the toe of Italy.
sicily.fact: Sicily is an island south of the Italian mainland.

veniceState.name: Republic of Venice
veniceState.hint: Look near the northern end of the Adriatic Sea.
veniceState.fact: Venice linked European markets with the eastern Mediterranean through maritime trade.

florence.name: Florence
florence.hint: Find the inland city in central northern Italy.
florence.fact: Florence was a major Renaissance centre. The Medici were prominent patrons of artists.

venice.name: Venice
venice.hint: Find the city at the northern end of the Adriatic Sea.
venice.fact: Venice’s location supported trade by sea and connections with inland Europe.

genoaCity.name: Genoa
genoaCity.hint: Find the port on Italy’s northwestern coast.
genoaCity.fact: Genoa’s wealth came in part from maritime trade and finance.

ottoman.name: Ottoman Empire
ottoman.hint: Look for the connected territories across southeastern Europe, Anatolia and parts of North Africa and western Asia.
ottoman.fact: This separate classroom reference shows Ottoman extent in 1683, well after the late-medieval map.

questions.q: Florence became the birthplace of Renaissance ______________________________.
What prominent banking family controlled Florence, and how did they support the Renaissance?
chips: They supported artists and commissioned works of art.

questions.q: Why is Venice ideally situated to become a trading hub?
chips: Venice is near the northern end of the Adriatic Sea.
Sea routes linked it with the eastern Mediterranean.
It connected sea trade with markets in Europe.

questions.q: List three reasons why Venice gained importance.
chips: Its position on sea trading routes.
Trade and contact with other cultures.
